question.problem: The professor of geometry notices that, on average, every batch of practice questions contains $6$ questions that cite the interior angle theorem in the solution. What is the probability that in the next batch of practice questions, there will be more than $5$ questions that cite the interior angle theorem in the solution? Round your answer to $3$ decimal places. You may assume that questions that cite the interior angle theorem in the solution occur independently and at a constant average rate.

current_example.problem: In a factory, $3$ machines, on average, suffer some fault during the course of a week. What is the probability that at least $2$ machines will register a fault next week? You may assume that faults occur independently and at a constant average rate.
current_example.worked_solution:
A Poisson random variable $X$ with rate $\lambda$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x) = \dfrac{\lambda^x e^{-\lambda}}{x!}
$$

Let $X$ be the number of machines with a fault in the factory. Since the average rate is $3$ faulty machines per week, and events occur independently and at a constant average rate, the number of machines with faults can be modeled as a Poisson random variable with rate $\lambda = 3,$ and we can write $X\sim \textrm{Po}(3).$

So, $X$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x) = \dfrac{3^x e^{-3}}{x!}
$$

To compute $P(X \geq 2),$ we will use the complement:

$$
P(X \geq 2) = 1 - P(X<  2)
$$

Computing the probability of the complement, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<2) & =P(X\in {0,1}) \\  & =f(0)+f(1) \\  & =\frac{{3}^{0}{e}^{-3}}{0!}+\frac{{3}^{1}{e}^{-3}}{1!} \\  & ≈0.199\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.

Therefore, the probability of at least $2$ machines registering a fault next week is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\ge 2) & =1-P(X<2) \\  & ≈1-0.199 \\  & ≈0.801\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.
